title: A transcription factor regulatory atlas for activity inference and perturbation prediction.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the Zenodo record 20779282 through its API: about 40 CSVs, each tissue file 5–53 MB, TFactprofiler_all.csv 86 MB, Table S1.csv 159 MB, human_chipatlas.csv 1.98 GB. Downloaded CollecTRI.csv (64,495 rows; source, target, weight, pmid) and TFactprofier_tonsil.csv (407,018 rows; source, target, weight, where weight is a fitted regression coefficient such as 0.105).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 2,606,176 interactions, 2,017 TFs (transcription factors) and 18,163 targets (I did not download all.csv). Knockdown benchmark results on KnockTF 2.0 and Replogle Perturb-seq (PRJNA831566, PRJNA1100571), and the comparisons with scFoundation and scGPT.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record is open with no login; two CSVs downloaded fine.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in the files: they hold only source/target/weight network edges. The only measured outcome, the expression change after a TF knockdown, lives in external data (KnockTF, Perturb-seq) and would have to be rebuilt as knockdown-minus-control contrasts.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene symbols are given directly, with no lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: The weight column is a unitless regularized-regression coefficient, and the files have no documented scale.

a5_enough_rows.note: That is the tonsil file, which I counted. The paper's 2.6M total for all.csv was not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~86 MB for all.csv; tissue files 5–53 MB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Small, except the 2 GB ChIP-Atlas snapshot.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checked against all.csv; the tissue files are subsets.

a8_label_provenance.note: The weights are outputs of the authors' cluster-wise regression on RNA-seq atlases. Predicting them means distilling their model, so the weights are not a measured label.

existing_models.name: TFActProfiler (this paper; zero-shot linear perturbation predictor)
existing_models.score_and_split: Correlation between predicted and observed knockdown changes on held-out unseen perturbations (10-fold over TFs); paper says higher than CollecTRI, scFoundation and scGPT embeddings.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Evaluating against nonlinear methods under matched conditions, and context-specific regulation in rare cell types.

existing_models.name: Linear model with pretrained perturbation embeddings (Ahlmann-Eltze et al., Nature Methods 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Matched or beat GEARS and scGPT on unseen single and double perturbations in Norman/Replogle data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Deep models do not yet beat simple linear baselines.

existing_models.name: GEARS / scGPT / scFoundation (via PerturBench and the BMC Genomics benchmark)
existing_models.score_and_split: Held-out perturbation splits; often no better than a mean-expression baseline.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Metric calibration; a later Nature Biotechnology 2026 paper argues deep models win on calibrated metrics.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a signed, prior-informed TF network predict knockdown responses in cell types it was not fitted on?

controls.positive_control: Knocking down a TF should lower that TF's own inferred activity.
controls.negative_control: Shuffling the edge targets of the network.

honest_claim_h3: Learning the weights would only reproduce the authors' regression, and perturbation prediction is a crowded benchmark field whose labels live in other papers' data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a signed map of which regulators control which genes to predict how gene expression changes when one regulator is knocked down.
plain_idea.train_on: TF–gene pairs with fitted regulatory coefficients (407,018 in the tonsil file; 2.6M overall per the paper), plus measured knockdown experiments from separate datasets.
plain_idea.predict: The expression change of every gene after a TF knockdown. The true answer comes from CRISPRi Perturb-seq or knockdown RNA-seq in other studies, not from this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs studying gene regulation could rank candidate TF knockdowns before running them. But this paper's own benchmark already covers that use.

more_or_better_data.why: The measured knockdown data (Replogle Perturb-seq, KnockTF) are the same public sets that GEARS, scGPT and the linear-baseline benchmarks already use; this paper adds only a fitted network.

confidence_score.why: TFActProfiler already reports an uncertainty-aware reliability score for TF activity.

models_beatable.why: Published benchmarks from 2025–2026 show deep models barely beat linear baselines, so gains would be marginal and disputed.

guaranteed_improvement.why: There is no new measured perturbation data here; the network is derived from the same public atlases.

ml_idea: Predict TF-knockdown transcriptome responses using the TFActProfiler signed network as a prior. Rejected: the labels are external, and the network weights are themselves model output.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because Part A failed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the Zenodo CSVs: they contain only fitted edge weights and no measured outcome column (done).

verdict_reason: The deposited data is a fitted TF–gene coefficient network, which is model output with no measured label (A2, A8). The real labels, knockdown responses, sit in external Perturb-seq data that a crowded, heavily benchmarked field already uses.
